answer: Airbnb's generated Bazel targets inferred dependencies mainly from Java/Kotlin/Scala source imports, so they sometimes missed runtime dependencies for classes loaded by reflection from configuration. Those reflective runtime dependencies are invisible to static-import analysis, so the generated targets omitted the artifacts that the deployable needed at runtime; Airbnb reported that roughly 100 of about 700 services initially failed startup/integration checks during Bazel-built deploy verification (largely reflective classes or version mismatches).
